title: Finite residue-field degrees in almost finite integral extensions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] that is a domain, meaning $1\ne0$ and $xy=0$ implies $x=0$ or $y=0$. Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ for its field of quotients $a/b$ with $a,b\in R$ and $b\ne0$. Let $F/K$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], meaning $F$ has finite dimension over $K$. Let $C$ be a subring of $F$ containing $R$, every element of which is integral over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For every prime ideal $Q$ of $C$, put $P=Q\cap R$. The induced field extension $\operatorname{Frac}(C/Q)/\operatorname{Frac}(R/P)$ has finite degree. Both fraction fields here mean fields of quotients of the indicated domains. No finite-generation assumption on $C$ over $R$ is imposed.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke, Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules, Proposition 4.8.5, printed p. 85, adapted there from Nagata, Local Rings (33.10); the domain case is written with residue fields as fraction fields of prime quotients. Read online in the author-hosted book at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a finite $K$-basis $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ of $F$. Each $x_i$ satisfies a monic equation $X^{r_i}+\sum_{h<r_i}c_{ih}X^h$ over $K$: powers of $x_i$ are linearly dependent in the finite-dimensional space $F$. Choose $0\ne a_i\in R$ clearing all coefficient denominators. Then $y_i=a_ix_i$ satisfies the monic equation $Y^{r_i}+\sum_{h<r_i}(a_i^{r_i-h}c_{ih})Y^h$ over $R$. Let $A=R[y_1,\ldots,y_d]\subset F$. By [lem-sc-finite-generated-integral-subring], $A$ is finite as an $R$-module, and by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] it is Noetherian. Moreover $\operatorname{Frac}(A)=F$: it contains $K$ and each $x_i=y_i/a_i$, hence their $K$-linear span.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; the finite integral-adjoin theorem is named by the first cited Mathlib leaf. The scaled-basis calculation is explicit.

proof.text: Let $D$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $F$. Then $A,C\subset D$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The inclusion $C\subset D$ is integral because a monic equation over $R$ is also one over $C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] lift the prescribed $Q\subset C$ to $N\subset D$ with $N\cap C=Q$. Set $\mathfrak a=N\cap A$; then $\mathfrak a\cap R=P$, and $C/Q\hookrightarrow D/N$. The ring $D$ is also the integral closure of $A$ in $F$. One inclusion follows by enlarging coefficients from $R$ to $A$; for the reverse, if $x\in F$ is integral over $A$, the subring $A[x]$ is integral over $A$ because the integral elements form a subring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] to $R\to A\to A[x]$ to obtain that $x$ is integral over $R$.

The images in $A/\mathfrak a$ of a finite $R$-module generating set of $A$ generate it over $R/P$: coefficients in $P$ vanish because $P A\subset\mathfrak a$. Thus $R/P\hookrightarrow A/\mathfrak a$ is a finite extension of domains. By [lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree], $k_1=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak a)$ is finite-dimensional over $k_0=\operatorname{Frac}(R/P)$.

source.place: Mathlib instFiniteDimensionalFractionRingOfFinite, Algebraic/Integral.lean:696–701; quotient generators and injection are written out.

proof.text: Put $U=A_{\mathfrak a}$ and $E=(A\setminus\mathfrak a)^{-1}D\subset F$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], $U$ is a Noetherian local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak aU$ and residue field $k_1$: modulo $\mathfrak a$, the denominators are exactly all nonzero elements of $A/\mathfrak a$. Its fraction field is $F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], $E$ is the integral closure of $U$ in $F$; localizing $F$ at these nonzero elements leaves $F$ itself. Define $\mathfrak q=\{d/s:d\in N,\ s\in A\setminus\mathfrak a\}\subset E$. Its quotient is the domain $(A\setminus\mathfrak a)^{-1}(D/N)$, so it is prime; its contraction to $U$ is $\mathfrak m$. The map $D/N\to E/\mathfrak q$ is injective and induces an isomorphism of fraction fields, since every $d/s$ is already a quotient of elements of $D/N$.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Tag 0307, lemma-integral-closure-localize. Prime localization and quotient fraction identifications are explicit.

proof.text: Let $H=\varprojlim_nU/\mathfrak m^n$ be the completion. The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $U/\mathfrak m=k_1$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and itself). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian] gives that $H$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak mH$-adically complete. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] it is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mH=\ker(H\to U/\mathfrak m)$ and residue field canonically $k_1$. It is therefore complete for its maximal-ideal topology. No reducedness or domain hypothesis on $H$ is used.

source.place: Tags 05GH, lemma-completion-Noetherian, and 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated; local-ring and residue comparison in the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-normalization-completed-branch-lift] to $U$, its birational integral closure $E$, and $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak m$. It supplies a minimal prime $\mathfrak p\subset H$, the integral closure $T$ of $H/\mathfrak p$ in its own fraction field, a compatible homomorphism $j:E\to T$, and a prime $M\subset T$ with $j^{-1}(M)=\mathfrak q$ and $M\cap(H/\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak n/\mathfrak p$. Thus $E/\mathfrak q\to T/M$ is injective. The composite $U\to E\to T\to T/M$ equals the map through $H/\mathfrak p$; consequently its induced map on $k_1$ is the same one as the completion residue identification in Step 5.

source.place: Lemma 4.8.3, component form recorded in the cited node; application to the Noetherian local domain U.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata], $H$ is Nagata; its statement says directly that $V=H/\mathfrak p$ is N-2. Taking the degree-one field extension of $\operatorname{Frac}(V)$ in [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] shows that $T$ is a finite $V$-module. Reducing a finite generating set modulo $M$ shows that $T/M$ is a finite module over $V/(\mathfrak n/\mathfrak p)=H/\mathfrak n=k_1$, because the contraction equality makes $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak p$ annihilate that quotient. Both rings are domains and the map from $k_1$ is injective. Applying [lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree] gives that $k_2=\operatorname{Frac}(T/M)$ is finite-dimensional over $k_1$.

source.place: Tag 032W, lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata; Tag 032F, definition-N; Mathlib fraction-field finiteness leaf. The quotient generators are explicit.

proof.text: The injections already obtained extend to fraction fields by $a/b\mapsto j(a)/j(b)$, since each nonzero denominator remains nonzero. They give compatible embeddings $k_0\subset\operatorname{Frac}(C/Q)\subset\operatorname{Frac}(D/N)\simeq\operatorname{Frac}(E/\mathfrak q)\subset k_2$. The products of a finite $k_0$-basis of $k_1$ and a finite $k_1$-basis of $k_2$ span $k_2$ over $k_0$. Therefore every $k_0$-linearly independent subset of $\operatorname{Frac}(C/Q)$ has cardinality at most that finite spanning-set size; the embedded subspace is finite-dimensional. This is precisely the claimed finite degree, with no module-finiteness assumption on $C$.

source.place: Elementary fraction extension, multiplication of finite spanning sets in a field tower, and finite-dimensional subspace argument.
